text: The subject, Arslan Ghani, a 36‑year‑old student with a declared monthly income of PKR 20,000, opened his HABB account on 2025‑03‑03. Within a ten‑day period (2026‑05‑02 to 2026‑05‑11) the account received eleven inbound IBFT transfers from ten different counterparties, each ranging from PKR 29,000 to PKR 86,000, totalling approximately PKR 720,000. The inbound activity triggered the MULE‑01 typology (score 360 > alert threshold 300) for “many distinct inbound counterparties” and “large share of inbound value leaves quickly.” Within the same window the account made two large outbound wallet transfers to the same QuickPay e‑wallet (PKR 285,000 on 2026‑05‑05 and PKR 287,000 on 2026‑05‑10) and three cash withdrawals (PKR 201,000, PKR 74,000 and PKR 74,000) via ATM, amounting to over PKR 560,000 of outflow. Fraud‑desk notes indicate two sender banks filed recall requests citing scam complaints on the inbound transfers, and the L2 analyst flagged the outbound wallet transfers as pending review with no customer contact. The rapid conversion of numerous small inbound funds into large cash and e‑wallet withdrawals, combined with external fraud alerts, is consistent with a money‑laundering mule operation and therefore warrants filing a Suspicious Transaction Report.
